walkthroughs.body_html:
Chromosomes, Genes & DNA — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Chromosomes, Genes & DNA brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Chromosomes, Genes & DNA.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does a gene code for?
options: Each gene codes for an organ or body part as a whole.
Both introns and exons are removed and the cell uses just the cap and tail.
Typically a polypeptide (protein) — through transcription to mRNA and translation by ribosomes.
A gene codes for a specific physical feature like eye colour directly.

mcqs.q: How are signals transmitted across a synapse between two neurones?
options: Via neurotransmitter chemicals released from the presynaptic neurone, which bind receptors on the postsynaptic neurone.
The electrical signal jumps directly from one neurone to the next across the synaptic gap.
Both introns and exons are removed and the cell uses just the cap and tail.
Neurones touch each other at synapses and pass current through direct contact.

mcqs.q: After pre-mRNA splicing in eukaryotes, which sequences remain in the mature mRNA?
options: Introns remain because they encode the protein; exons are removed as junk.
Neurones touch each other at synapses and pass current through direct contact.
Exons remain; introns are removed.
Both introns and exons are removed and the cell uses just the cap and tail.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Chromosome”?
options: Polymer of nucleotides forming a double helix; carries genetic information in the bases.
Four types: A pairs with T, C pairs with G — complementary base pairing.
The entire genetic material of an organism.
Long DNA molecule packaged with proteins.

A whole chromosome
A complete organism

mcqs.q: A mutation changes one base in a gene but the protein produced is unchanged. Which is the best explanation?
options: The change still coded for the same amino acid.
Mutations can never change a protein.
The gene was not used to make protein.
The cell repaired the DNA back to a different sequence.
